title: Peptide-to-Protein Data Aggregation Using Fisher’s Method in Chemical Proteomics
author: Lyu, Hezheng
materials:
The first data set used for testing Fisher’s-based
approach
consisted of expression (FITExP) proteomic data from drug-treated
MCF-7 cells extracted from the ProTargetMiner database. Briefly, MCF-7 cells were exposed for 48 h to
IC50 concentrations of nine anticancer compounds representing
diverse mechanisms of action. For FoM calculations, we used the known
targets of bortezomib (PSMB1 and PSMB5) and raltitrexed (TYMS and
FPGS). The second data set was a solubility (PISA) assay from the ThermoTargetMiner database and originated from A549 cell lysate treated with different
drugs against lung cancer. For FoM determination, we used the known
targets of vorinostat (targets: HDACs), everolimus (target: MTOR)
and olaparib (targets: PARP1, PARP2, and AKR1C3). The third data set
was an automated PISA assay (OPTI-PISA) obtained from A549 cell lysates treated with 10 μM methotrexate
(MTX, target: DHFR), staurosporine (targets: kinases), or ganetespib
(targets: HSP90s). The last data set comprised the combined PISA-expression proteomics profile of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU)-resistant
versus 5FU-sensitive SW480 cells, with the 5FU targets of TYMS used
for FoM calculations.

steps.title: Generate LC‑MS/MS datasets
steps.instruction: Treat MCF‑7 cells with IC50 concentrations of nine anticancer compounds for 48 h and A549 cell lysates with 10 μM methotrexate (or staurosporine, ganetespib) using expression (FITExP), solubility (PISA), OPTI‑PISA, AFDIP and HOLSER assays; digest proteins with trypsin, label peptides with TMT multiplexing, and acquire raw LC‑MS/MS files.

steps.title: Process raw LC‑MS/MS files
steps.instruction: Analyze each raw LC‑MS/MS file with MaxQuant (MQ) and/or Proteome Discoverer (PD) to generate peptide‑level and protein‑level output tables; if both programs are used, keep results from both for downstream analysis.

steps.title: Remove contaminants and non‑unique peptides
steps.instruction: Exclude any peptide or protein assigned to contaminant proteins or reversed sequences and discard peptides that are not uniquely assigned to a single protein.

steps.title: Group peptides by protein and normalize
steps.instruction: Group the remaining peptides by their protein IDs and normalize each peptide’s abundance to the total ion count within its TMT channel.

steps.title: Calculate fold changes
steps.instruction: For expression (FITExP) and solubility (PISA) datasets, compute fold changes directly from protein abundances; for validation datasets (AFDIP and HOLSER), compute fold changes from the abundances of the top four peptides per protein.

steps.title: Filter protein lists
steps.instruction: Remove proteins identified only with modified peptides; discard proteins with more than one missing value among biological replicates (n ≥ 3) per condition; discard proteins supported by fewer than two peptides.

steps.title: Impute missing values (PISA‑Expression)
steps.instruction: For the PISA‑Expression dataset, replace any remaining missing normalized abundances with the average normalized abundance of that protein across the other replicates.

steps.title: Cross‑validate protein lists
steps.instruction: Compare the protein lists obtained from peptide‑level and protein‑level analyses and retain only proteins that appear in both lists.

steps.title: Statistical testing
steps.instruction: Perform a two‑tailed unpaired Student’s t‑test for each peptide and protein comparing normalized abundances of treated versus control samples; calculate fold change as the ratio of median treated abundance to median control abundance; for PISA, expression and OPTI‑PISA retain only peptides with consistent fold‑change direction; apply Benjamini–Hochberg correction to all p‑values.

steps.title: Rank peptides and compute composite score
steps.instruction: Within each protein, rank peptides by p‑value, fold change, or by the composite score –log10(p‑value) × |log2(fold change)|.

steps.title: Select top N peptides per protein
steps.instruction: For each protein, select either all peptides or the top N peptides (N = 2, 3, 4, 5, 6). If N exceeds the number of available peptides, handle missing p‑values by (i) using only the available p‑values (no imputation) or (ii) imputing the average p‑value of the existing peptides for that protein.

steps.title: Calculate X² statistic
steps.instruction: Compute X² = ‑2 ∑_{i=1}^{N} ln(p_i) for the selected peptides of each protein.

steps.title: Compute combined protein p‑value
steps.instruction: In R, use pchisq(X², df = 2 N, lower.tail = FALSE) to obtain the one‑tailed probability of observing an X² equal to or greater than the observed value; this is the combined protein p‑value.

steps.title: Derive protein ranking score
steps.instruction: For each protein, calculate a score = –log10(combined p‑value) × |log2(fold change)| (or use the same composite formula with peptide‑level p‑values when appropriate).

steps.title: Rescale protein ranks
steps.instruction: Sort proteins by the score in descending order and rescale their rank positions to a uniform range of 1–8000 to enable comparison across datasets of different proteome depth.

steps.title: Calculate Figure of Merit per drug
steps.instruction: For each drug (except staurosporine), compute FoM = ∑_{k=1}^{n} 1,000,000 / RankFk, where RankFk is the rescaled rank of the k‑th known target (n = number of known targets). For staurosporine, count the number of kinases among the top 100 ranked proteins and use this count as the FoM.

steps.title: Renormalize and sum FoM values
steps.instruction: For a given N, renormalize each dataset’s FoM to a 1–10 scale and sum the renormalized FoM values across all datasets to obtain the final score for the evaluated Fisher‑based strategy.
